name: US National Weather Service: the national hazards map (weather.gov)

frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

capture_note: Not captured yet: asked of incident.archivist@ on 11 November 2026 (the callouts stand on this agent's own render; the frame stays empty and the link stands).
licence_for_showing_the_screenshot: US government work, public domain (third-party map tiles excepted): a screenshot may be shown.
summary: The front page of a national service is its hazards map: every county and every coastal water of the country, coloured by the hazard in force, with the time the map was made printed on the map and a legend that lists only the hazards in force. Above it, the day's national headline in three sentences. Colour here means the kind of hazard, not how severe it is.

callouts.title: The national headline, in words
callouts.does_well: "Storm System to Move Across the Ohio Valley to the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast", then two sentences and "Read More": the forecasters' own summary sits above every map.
callouts.fed_by: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/communiques.json (the current communiqué's subject and first sentence, quoted)

callouts.title: One row of doors
callouts.does_well: Active alerts, forecast maps, radar, rivers and rainfall, air quality, satellite, current: seven words, each a view of the same country.

callouts.title: The time is on the map
callouts.does_well: "Created: 11/11/26 at 03:38 UTC" is drawn inside the image, so a copy of the map carries its own time.
callouts.fed_by: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/warnings.json (read_utc), drawn inside our own strip and map

callouts.title: Everything in force, on one map
callouts.does_well: Counties and marine zones are white until something is in force; a click on any of them opens the alerts for that place.
callouts.fed_by: our own redraw from IPMA's JSON; district shapes from an open source

callouts.title: A legend of what is in force only
callouts.does_well: Eighteen kinds of alert were listed at this read, each a link to its own list: the legend is built from the map, not printed whole.
callouts.fed_by: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/warnings.json (the levels and hazards present at this read)

callouts.title: The same as data, under the map
callouts.does_well: "Public Alerts in XML/CAP v1.2 and ATOM Formats": one link, directly beneath the picture.
callouts.fed_by: api/v1/index.json and the warnings file's own address

limits: Colours are by kind of alert (a gale warning, a flood advisory), so the map does not show at a glance which is the most severe. No alert was opened.
